# TinyRustLM

> TinyRustLM.MiRust.com is the TinyRustLM developer portal: a plain PHP project website explaining a zero-dependency Rust/WebAssembly browser-local small language model runtime, an absorbed legacy runtime documentation archive, custom .slm artifacts, strict validation, quantized execution, adapter sidecars, selector registries, deterministic test evidence, UAI file memory, durable reports, and a direct project contact route for Mike Kappel.

## Core Pages

- [Overview](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/): Project summary, constraints, runtime surfaces, and deployment posture.
- [NuGet SDK](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/developer-portal/): Protected TinyRustLM SDK packaging in `SLMComposer.com` exposes only `.slm` validation/inspection, native-backed runtime harness operations, UAIX `.uai` memory/persona package planning and inspection, metadata-bound P2P share/import workflows with local signed-manifest verification, local manifest-piece verification, `.slm` assembly, typed announcement/catalog application and inspection, announcement JSON handoff helpers, receipt sidecars, and receipt-sidecar inspection, and .NET wrappers through `TinyRustLM.Abstractions`, `TinyRustLM.Core`, `TinyRustLM.P2P`, and `TinyRustLM.Memory`; the local UAIX Browser feed emits `UAIX.Browser.Core.Abstractions`, `UAIX.Browser.p2pLLM.Runtime`, `UAIX.Browser.p2pRuntime.P2P`, `UAIX.Browser.Memory`, and controlled `UAIX.Browser.p2pLLM.Conversion`; release verification includes package-private-surface inspection, source/debug/generated-output/local-path leakage audits, clean temporary consumer smoke, required metadata/search-term/XML documentation package audits through `tinyrustlm.nuget.package_audit.v0`, native-asset gating, dry-run publish-set audits, publish-plan evidence bound to `SHA256SUMS-TinyRustLM-<version>.txt`, readiness evidence with top-level package/symbol counts and SHA256SUMS binding fields, feed-current and SHA256SUMS-bound package-byte verification, and no push secrets in monitor reports.
- [Memory harness](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/developer-portal/): `TinyRustLM.Memory` advanced-persona inspection reports `PersonaDimensions`, `PersonaDimensionsValid`, and `PersonaDimensionWarningCount` for `depth_level_0_to_10`, disclosure boundary, source confidence, and non-inference rule evidence.
- Package-audit reports now record declared package-file entries and package documentation entries, expose `missing_package_file_count`, and fail when declared README/license files are missing from `.nupkg` contents.
- Package-audit reports also record expected packaged documentation source hashes and fail when packaged README/license/package docs do not byte-match the current `docs/nuget` source files.
- Package-audit reports now enforce the exact source-versioned package set: `TinyRustLM.Abstractions`, `TinyRustLM.Core`, `TinyRustLM.P2P`, and `TinyRustLM.Memory`; missing or unexpected `TinyRustLM*.nupkg` files fail before publish.
- Package-audit reports now enforce matching `.snupkg` symbol package files; publish-plan evidence records `symbol_package_count` and `symbol_publish_mode=explicit_snupkg_push_after_primary_package`, and the SHA256SUMS manifest is symbol-hash-bound so symbols stay bound to the audited SDK release. NuGet Package Manager generally lists installable `.nupkg` packages; each `.snupkg` is a debug-symbol sidecar verified through the local folder feed, workflow artifacts, `SymbolsPackage`/PDB evidence, SHA256SUMS membership, publish-plan hashes, and feed-hash reports.
- Package-audit reports now enforce required NuGet search terms including `UAIX.Browser`, `p2pRuntime`, `p2pLLM`, `MiniModel`, `.slm`, `.uai`, `memory`, `ai-memory`, and `persona`.
- The local UAIX Browser folder feed has a `uaix.browser.nuget.feed_audit.v0` verifier for branded package IDs, matching `.snupkg` symbol packages, `SymbolsPackage` metadata, PDB evidence, search metadata, dependency graph, SHA256SUMS membership, and local-path leakage.
- The Browser package lane has an audited `publish-browser-nuget.ps1` dry run that requires `uaix.browser.nuget.feed_audit.v0`, `SHA256SUMS-UAIX.Browser-<version>.txt`, five `.nupkg` files, and five `.snupkg` files, then writes `uaix-browser-nuget-publish-plan.json` with schema `uaix.browser.nuget.publish_plan.v0`.
- The UAIX Browser feed-current monitor sets `TINYRUSTLM_FEED_PACKAGE_IDS` to the five `UAIX.Browser.*` package IDs, writes `uaix-browser-nuget-feed-current.json`, and can run on schedule with `UAIX_BROWSER_NUGET_MONITOR_VERIFY_CURRENT=true`.
- The branded Browser release workflow `.github/workflows/release-browser-nuget.yml` publishes the five-package lane, gates publication with `audit-browser-nuget-release-readiness.ps1`, writes `uaix-browser-nuget-release-readiness.json` with schema `uaix.browser.nuget.release_readiness.v0`, skips redundant pushes when the feed is already `published_current`, blocks `blocked_remote_hash_mismatch` when an immutable feed version has different bytes, requires `uaix-browser-nuget-feed-current.json` and `uaix-browser-nuget-feed-hashes.json`, and can smoke `UAIX.Browser.p2pLLM.Runtime` plus `UAIX.Browser.p2pRuntime.P2P` through configurable consumer verification. If NuGet.org already lists the declared version with different bytes, bump `VersionPrefix` before publishing corrected Browser packages.
- Package-audit reports also fail if any package's nuspec `id` or `version` differs from its protected filename and the source-declared package version.
- Package-audit reports also enforce the public NuGet dependency graph: Abstractions has no package dependencies, Core depends only on same-version Abstractions, and P2P plus Memory depend only on same-version Abstractions and Core.
- Package-audit dependency checks also require protected package references to retain `exclude=Build,Analyzers` metadata.
- Package-audit reports also enforce native asset placement: native runtime entries are allowed only in Core, while Abstractions, P2P, and Memory remain managed API/metadata packages.
- Package-audit reports also allow only the expected Core native filenames: `tinyrustlm_native.dll` for Windows, `libtinyrustlm_native.so` for Linux, and `libtinyrustlm_native.dylib` for macOS.
- Package-audit reports also enforce a narrow package-entry allow-list: NuGet metadata, nuspec, README/license, package docs, `lib/net8.0` DLL/XML outputs, and approved Core native assets.
- Package-audit reports also enforce the public API surface from packaged XML docs, failing if Abstractions/Core/P2P/Memory expose managed members outside the approved SDK contract.
- Post-pack package tests also enforce the binary public surface, failing if exported types, public constructor arity, DTO properties, or declared workflow methods drift outside the approved SDK contract.
- NuGet P2P announcement URL validation accepts HTTPS or explicit-port loopback HTTP only, validates `PublicBaseUrl` directly before writing announcements, and rejects credentials, whitespace, query strings, fragments, backslashes, dot-segment traversal, and encoded traversal before metadata is trusted. Received catalogs deduplicate honest announcement replays but reject conflicting same-peer/same-manifest metadata before mutation; `InspectAnnouncementCatalog` reports catalog SHA/count/byte evidence and rejects catalog JSON above 4 MiB before parsing.
- MiniModel signed-manifest verification now accepts only `signature.kind=external-signature-v0`, rejects comments and unsafe or missing key routes, requires `signature.payload_sha256` to match the canonical sorted non-signature manifest body, and prints the canonical digest from `minimodel verify-manifest` for publisher review. `minimodel verify-signed-manifest <manifest> <public-key-json>` now performs local Ed25519 verification against metadata-only `minimodel.public_key.v0` public-key JSON; transparency-log inclusion and remote key-discovery policy remain future work.
- The protected NuGet P2P SDK exposes `VerifySignedManifest` / `VerifySignedManifestJson` for local `tinyrustlm.p2p_signed_manifest.v0` envelopes against metadata-only `minimodel.public_key.v0` public-key JSON; it checks wrapped manifest validity, canonical payload SHA-256, `external-signature-v0`, `ed25519-base64:` signature bytes, matching publisher/key/route/SHA usage, and `revoked=false` while signing, remote key discovery, transparency-log checks, and publisher services remain outside the package.
- MiniModel catalog/feed inspection now reports exact metadata byte counts plus SHA-256 values and rejects catalog or peer-source announcement feed JSON above 4 MiB before parsing. TinyRustLM's mapped public-root `hf-peer-announcement-budget-ui` smoke proves oversized local announcement/feed files are rejected at the browser metadata budget before JSON parse or peer-source application, and `hf-catalog-announcement-route-budget-ui` proves oversized catalog-declared feed routes report `Peer-source announcement metadata exceeded browser budget`, stay at `Set Peer URL`, and save no peer import kit.
- NuGet SDK wrapper update: `TinyRustLmRuntimeFactory.GetVersion()` exposes native SDK/ABI version data, `PrepareLocalShareKit` returns typed `P2PShareKitReport`, `ExportShareMetadata` returns typed `P2PShareMetadata`, `VerifySignedManifest` returns typed `P2PSignedManifestVerification`, `ValidateAnnouncement` / `ApplyReceivedAnnouncement` return typed `P2PAnnouncement` / `P2PAnnouncementCatalog` records, `InspectAnnouncementCatalog` returns typed `P2PAnnouncementCatalogInspection`, and `PrepareLocalShareKitJson` / `ExportShareMetadataJson` / `VerifySignedManifestJson` / `ValidateAnnouncementJson` / `ApplyReceivedAnnouncementJson` / `InspectAnnouncementCatalogJson` remain for exact JSON handoff documents. The .NET wrapper and native public runtime SDK validate generation options before runtime mutation; direct native callers receive `invalid_generation_options` for invalid token count, sampler cap, or sampling probability values. The .NET wrapper also rejects embedded NUL characters in native-bound strings before P/Invoke, preserves empty managed strings as native empty strings rather than null pointers, validates `PrepareShareKitRequest` shape before native JSON serialization, rejecting missing model/output paths and piece sizes outside 1 KiB through 16 MiB as managed argument errors, and mirrors Rust P2P JSON byte budgets before native calls for manifests or signed-manifest envelopes, public-key JSON, announcements, receipts, and announcement catalogs.
- NuGet publication status as of 2026-07-06: local package-folder verification passes for version `0.1.2`, but NuGet.org reports zero listed versions for `TinyRustLM.Abstractions`, `TinyRustLM.Core`, `TinyRustLM.P2P`, and `TinyRustLM.Memory`; the current release-readiness report is `blocked_missing_api_key`; public NuGet.org availability is incomplete until authenticated publish plus feed-current and SHA256SUMS-bound feed-hash verification passes.
- Current local release-gate evidence for 2026-07-06 is green for `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, and `eng\verify-package.ps1`; the package verifier itself now runs workspace rustfmt and clippy before Rust tests, rebuilt the native bridge, ran Rust/.NET tests, packed the four protected packages, wrote the package audit with required search-term evidence, and passed clean consumer `.slm` runtime plus UAIX memory/persona and P2P share/import/receipt smoke from local package references.
- TinyRustLM UI verification now writes `tinyrustlm.ui_verification.v0` evidence through `eng\verify-tinyrustlm-ui.ps1 -RunBrowserSmoke` and its Bash parity script; CI runs the static browser harness, loopback HTTP harness, and `source-options-ui`, `local-connect-approval-ui`, `local-connect-endpoint-ui`, and `local-connect-rust-endpoint-ui` browser smokes for Local .slm, Hugging Face, P2P import, Advanced tools, Local Connect approval presets, endpoint app inventory, digest-bound dry-run action flow, and the actual Rust `serve-approval-endpoint` path.
- TinyRustLM.com root verification writes `tinyrustlm.public_root_verification.v0` evidence through `eng\verify-tinyrustlm-public-root.ps1` and `eng/verify-tinyrustlm-public-root.sh`; it serves mapped `http://tinyrustlm.com:<port>/` with `tinyrustlm.com-loopback-browser-smoke`, runs `public-local-only`, `catalog-local-import`, `local-import-ambiguous-selection`, `peer-url-unsafe-ui`, `local-connect-approval-ui`, `local-connect-endpoint-ui`, and `local-connect-rust-endpoint-ui`, and writes `tinyrustlm-public-root-verification.json`.
- [Peer Companion Inventory](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/browser-runtime/): Generated local P2P share kits write and inspect metadata-only `minimodel.peer_companion_inventory.v0` files for consenting known-peer flows, binding companion state, receipt ledger, piece-store byte/quota/SHA-256 evidence, contact cards, and a `ready-after-rust-reverify` serve plan without model bytes.
- [Inventory Import UI](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/browser-runtime/): TinyRustLM can load local peer companion inventory JSON in simple/advanced P2P panels, reject no-byte-boundary and serve-plan drift, show Rust-reverify-required summary metadata with the peer URL and peer status route, and fill/persist the Known peer URL for later P2P import request/script generation without remote requests. Mapped public-root browser-smoke `hf-peer-companion-inventory-ui` proves that inventory-derived peer URL reaches the downloaded P2P import request/script for proof-ready Hugging Face rows.
- [Architecture](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/architecture/): System map covering the static browser UI, Rust/WASM runtime, offline packer, local server, harness, and claim boundaries.
- [Runtime](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/runtime/): Rust/WASM runtime responsibilities, memory transfer, generation, diagnostics, and explicit error states.
- [.slm Format](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/slm-format/): Custom model artifact contract for header, tensor directory, tokenizer metadata, quantization fields, and checksum validation.
- [Quantization](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/quantization/): f32, q8_0, and q4_0 memory math under the 33,554,432-byte browser selector budget.

- Generated conversion/share kits run `inspect-peer-source-announcement-feed` immediately after writing `peer-source-announcements.v0.json`; feed-bound catalog snapshots are created only after that Rust preflight passes. They also run `inspect-catalog-snapshot` after writing normal and feed-bound `models.v0.json` snapshots, `inspect-peer-companion-state` after writing companion handoff state, `inspect-peer-contact-book` after writing the contact-book handoff, `inspect-import-receipt-ledger` after writing sender-side `import-receipts.v0.json`, and `inspect-peer-companion-inventory` after writing companion inventory metadata. Feed/catalog inspectors report exact byte/SHA evidence and reject JSON above 4 MiB before parsing. Generated share kits honor `MINIMODEL_KNOWN_PEER_BASE_URL` for reviewed local automation, and source plus mapped public-root `share-metadata-kit-exec` executes the exact browser-downloaded `.minimodel-share-kit.ps1`, verifies MiniModel metadata plus local receipt, sender-side receipt-ledger, feed, catalog, companion-state validation PASS output, contact-card/contact-book outputs, and companion-inventory validation PASS output, starts local companion serving, and runs `check-peer-status` without fetching peer-piece or artifact bytes.
- Peer contact books are supported beside peer contact cards: TinyRustLM can load local `minimodel.peer_contact_book.v0` metadata, validate embedded card SHA-256s, duplicate peer rejection, and no-model-byte/no-peer-piece/no-catalog-claim boundaries, render all reviewed peers as a chooser, set Known peer URL from the selected reviewed peer, and `hf-peer-contact-book-ui` / `hf-peer-contact-book-reject-ui` prove accept/reject behavior. Generated conversion/share kits now write and inspect those books when `KnownPeerBaseUrl` is set.
- Generated P2P import scripts run MiniModel `inspect-peer-import-request` before `check-peer-status`, then `inspect-peer-status-check` before preflight, followed by saved-preflight inspection, import, `inspect-import-receipt`, `inspect-peer-import-receipt` with receipt-after-preflight timestamp ordering, `write-import-receipt-ledger`, `inspect-import-receipt-ledger`, and local `.slm` browser import.
- Known peer URLs must be direct `http://` peer URLs with plain DNS/IPv4 host text and safe absolute paths; query strings, fragments, traversal paths, whitespace/control paths, non-plain host text, canonical project/Hugging Face hosts, `www` aliases, subdomains, and trailing DNS-root-dot variants fail before TinyRustLM saves the URL or writes generated handoff scripts. The `peer-url-unsafe-ui` smoke proves this on source and mapped public-host roots.
- `inspect-gguf`, `plan-gguf-source`, `extract-gguf-source`, and `convert-gguf-trained` now provide a Rust GGUF intake and F32/F16/BF16/Q2_K/Q3_K/Q4_0/Q4_1/Q4_K/Q5_0/Q5_1/Q5_K/Q6_K/Q8_0/Q8_1/Q8_K conversion path: F32 tensors copy into raw source, F16/BF16 tensors decode to raw f32, Q2_K/Q3_K/Q4_0/Q4_1/Q4_K/Q5_0/Q5_1/Q5_K/Q6_K/Q8_0/Q8_1/Q8_K blocks dequantize to raw f32, the source manifest is validated, and the existing trained-source converter writes `.slm`; GGUF conversion still requires supported tensor names/shapes, tokenizer token-count compatibility, and Rust validation before .slm import; `plan-gguf-source` fails closed when `tokenizer.ggml.tokens` contradicts the target vocab, and BPE source shapes import `tokenizer.ggml.tokens`/`tokenizer.ggml.merges` into the raw source manifest when both are declared.
- Source `gguf_cli` coverage proves BPE GGUF token/merge rows are preserved into `source.manifest`, and that tokenizer vocab-count drift fails closed through `plan-gguf-source` before conversion.
- Local Connect approvals expose `Ask every time`, `Always approve selected`, `Trust Browsers + Email`, and high-risk `Full local-control lab mode`; category warnings cover browsers, email apps, docs/office, files/folders, terminal/scripts, and passwords/payments/settings, approved app names stay in local storage, the browser renders a `tinyrustlm.local_connect_approval_policy.v0` `policy_version=2` JSON preview with `full_control_non_sensitive_machine_acknowledged` and category-bound `approved_app_bindings`, can save `tinyrustlm-local-connect-policy.v0.json` without sending it to project servers, and Rust `tinyrustlm-local-connect` validates that policy, rejects unacknowledged full-control policies, rejects binding drift and terminal/password app-level always approvals, and can run a loopback `serve-approval-endpoint` health/categories/apps/decision/action API that revalidates the watched policy file before each request, applies valid saved-policy replacements without restart, and fails closed with `policy-reload-failed` when the watched file is invalid. Endpoint identity is hash-bound with canonical policy SHA-256 in `policy_sha256`; `/v0/apps` uses bounded local app-name discovery plus common fallbacks, marks known rows as `Found locally`, exposes names/category/risk/decision only with `inventory_paths_exposed=false`, advertises `app_inventory_policy=bounded-name-discovery-no-paths-v1`, `app_inventory_path_exposure=never`, `app_approval_binding_policy=app-and-category-v1`, and `action_execution_policy=typed-action-dry-run-default-v1`, gives each row local controls to always approve the app, always approve its category, or block the category before saving a refreshed endpoint policy JSON over the watched file, disables app-level approval for terminal/password rows, and recomputes visible row decisions when acknowledged full local-control lab mode is selected while explicit blocks stay denied; `/v0/decision` and `/v0/action` both prevent approved app names from authorizing requests outside the app's bound category; and `/v0/action` requires the same digest in `x-tinyrustlm-policy-sha256`, dry-runs by default, includes the binding/execution contract IDs in `action_request_sha256`, and limits execution to typed native-opener actions.
- Local Connect `/v0/action` also returns `action_request_sha256`; CLI `execute-action` prints `action.request_sha256`, and browser validation requires a valid request fingerprint plus the `app-and-category-v1` / `typed-action-dry-run-default-v1` contract IDs before trusting action dry-run evidence.
- The local browser picker can select a peer-assembled `.slm` with its `.minimodel-receipt` sidecar; TinyRustLM validates receipt shape, strict UTC timestamp, model id, manifest/artifact SHA-256 values, artifact byte count, SLM shape/quantization/evidence fields, `import.next_gate`, peer path hints, peer base URL, companion-state URL/status, fixed chunk mode, final receiver-validation contract gates, peer-transfer evidence, companion metadata flag, and no-project-server-byte flags before rendering `minimodel-p2p-import-receipt` provenance. After Rust/WASM acceptance it surfaces receipt hash/time, sidecar name, manifest SHA-256, receiver-validation status, peer URL, companion status, chunk count, artifact SHA-256, and browser-load readiness in the Provenance panel. It accepts exactly one `.slm` and at most one receipt sidecar, rejecting ambiguous selections instead of guessing.
- Receipt-drift smoke mutates the sidecar artifact SHA-256, `peer_companion_state_metadata_fetched`, `receiver_validation.import_receipt_required_before_browser_load`, `receiver_validation_contract.status`, and `receipt.created_utc`, proving TinyRustLM reports the expected MiniModel receipt error before selecting the local model.
- Import receipt ledgers are browser metadata only: the simple P2P panel and Advanced source details load `minimodel.import_receipt_ledger.v0`, validate no-byte boundaries, counts, SHA-256 fields, duplicate receipt paths, peer-import gates, and direct peer URL shape, show `Rust reverify required`, and leave `minimodel inspect-import-receipt-ledger` as the local trust gate. Generated P2P import scripts write `import-receipts.v0.json` and inspect it before browser import.
- Peer status checks are browser metadata only: the simple P2P panel and Advanced source details load `minimodel.peer_status_check`, validate route/manifest/artifact/piece SHA-256 fields plus no-peer-piece/no-artifact-byte boundaries, show peer URL, piece count, companion route, report SHA-256, and `Rust reverify required`; generated receiver scripts revalidate saved reports with MiniModel `inspect-peer-status-check`, and `peer-status-check-ui` proves browser drift rejection without remote requests.
- The local `Peer-source announcement/feed JSON` picker accepts full `peer-source-announcements.v0.json` feed envelopes as well as single announcements; `hf-peer-announcement-ui` proves the feed file path applies a matching peer source before `P2P Import`, `hf-peer-announcement-reject-ui` proves duplicate same-model/same-peer feeds fail closed at `Set Peer URL` without saving a peer import kit, `hf-peer-announcement-budget-ui` proves oversized local feeds fail before parse/application, `hf-catalog-announcement-route-budget-ui` proves oversized catalog-declared feed routes fail closed with no peer import kit, and MiniModel `inspect-peer-source-announcement-feed` covers the matching Rust preflight for existing feeds.
- Root-package public-host local import smoke proves TinyRustLM.com can import a real user-selected fixture `.slm`, verify SHA-256/provenance, run Rust/WASM generation, and reject duplicate `.slm` or duplicate receipt selections while loading only app/runtime assets from the project host.
- Root-package public-host share-kit smoke proves the packaged TinyRustLM.com root can save and execute the exact local P2P share kit, write and inspect a local import receipt plus sender-side receipt ledger, start local MiniModel companion serving only after both the printed serve hint and helper inspect companion state, and validate peer-status metadata without fetching peer-piece or artifact bytes.
- Root-package public-host share-metadata receiver smoke proves the packaged TinyRustLM.com root rejects chunk-list drift and wrong local `.slm` artifacts, keeps valid local share metadata at `Use Metadata`, loads/generates from the matching local `.slm`, and makes only app/runtime network requests.
- Root-package public-host P2P smoke proves the packaged TinyRustLM.com root can complete the `hf-p2p-import-kit-exec` converted-once-to-P2P path with catalog/manifest/feed metadata, a consenting path-prefixed MiniModel peer at `http://127.0.0.1:8123/peer-pieces/`, peer-status/status-check-inspection/preflight/preflight-inspection/import verification, receipt-chain inspection, generated receipt-ledger inspection, receipt-matched `.slm` output, local browser import, and Rust/WASM generation, and `hf-p2p-import-receipt-reject` proves receipt artifact SHA, companion metadata, receiver-validation gate, receiver-validation contract status, and timestamp drift fail closed.
- Peer URL, peer contact card/book, and P2P toggle refreshes preserve accepted Hugging Face `.safetensors` source metadata, so source-backed `Start Conversion` / `Review Conversion` fallbacks remain available after P2P handoffs.
- Source `hf-search-ui` coverage captures three Hugging Face conversion-kit branches: the normal single-file `.safetensors` `Start Conversion` request/script/README, the large two-shard `.safetensors` `Review Conversion` request/script/README with `source_input_mode=safetensors-shard-directory`, and the GGUF `Review Conversion` request/script/README with `source_format=gguf`, `request_inspect_shape=inspect-huggingface-conversion-request`, `TINYRUSTLM_SOURCE_GGUF`, `inspect-gguf`, `plan-gguf-source`, `convert-gguf-trained`, reviewed F32/F16/BF16/Q2_K/Q3_K/Q4_0/Q4_1/Q4_K/Q5_0/Q5_1/Q5_K/Q6_K/Q8_0/Q8_1/Q8_K guidance, GGUF tensor-routing and tokenizer boundary warnings, SHA-256/byte hints, and no Hugging Face `/resolve/` byte fetch.
- `inspect-huggingface-conversion-request` writes a source-byte-free `tinyrustlm-conversion.request.inspect` report with request SHA-256, source format, source input mode, expected safetensors/GGUF file rows, no-project-server byte flags, and the required next gate; `convert-huggingface-request` preflight evidence records `request_sha256`, successful conversion receipts record `output_slm_sha256` plus `output_manifest_sha256`, and `inspect-huggingface-conversion-receipt` revalidates the request/preflight/receipt/manifest chain before MiniModel sharing.
- Source `hf-conversion-kit-exec` executes all three generated conversion branches, including sharded `.safetensors` `Review Conversion` against a reviewed deterministic shard directory with local shard hash/byte evidence and GGUF `Review Conversion` against a reviewed deterministic Q3_K GGUF fixture; it verifies the request-inspection report, Rust `.slm` conversion, GGUF inspect/plan/dequant-q3_k evidence, MiniModel metadata outputs, local import receipt plus receipt-ledger inspection, peer contact book inspection, peer companion inventory inspection, and serve-helper companion-state inspection without project-server model bytes.
- Source `hf-conversion-kit-exec` also executes the exact generated `Review Conversion` script against unreconciled mismatched shard metadata and proves request inspection passes while Rust fails closed with `source_contract_status=fail`, no `.slm`, no receipt, and no MiniModel peer-share output.

## Preserved Reports

- [Engineering Tiny Language Models for Deterministic WebAssembly and Rust Runtimes](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/docs/reports/tiny-language-models-for-wasm.md): Core tiny-model feasibility, micro-model tiers, quantization constraints, deterministic WASM smoke testing, and Rust/WASM runtime pressure.
- [Architecting Minimalist Neural Inference in WebAssembly](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/docs/reports/rust-wasm-neural-model-patterns.md): WASM heap planning, zero-copy tensor views, tokenizer data structures, SIMD matrix-vector kernels, and deterministic neural inference design.
- [Architecture and Engineering of TinyRustLM](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/docs/reports/understanding-tinyrustlm-creation-and-purpose.md): Primary TinyRustLM explanation: browser-local runtime, .slm format, q8/q4 quantization, adapters, selector registries, and offline model breeding.
- [Tiny Language Models for Rust/WASM](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/docs/reports/tiny-language-models-for-rust-wasm.md): Candidate model analysis, 33.5 MB budget math, Llama and GPT-NeoX topology notes, tokenizer constraints, and converter requirements.
- [GGUF MiRust All Source Review Bundle](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/docs/reports/gguf-mirust-all-source-review-bundle.txt): Large source review bundle containing the TinyRustLM source inventory, hot .uai memory files, docs, runtime, packer, harness, and model-breeding artifacts.
- [Memory Systems Domains Research](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/docs/reports/memory-systems-domains-research.md): Background research on AI memory domains, UAIX-style short-term handoff, long-term governed memory, and machine-readable knowledge routing.
- [Future-Proof Native HTML5 Techniques](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/docs/reports/future-proof-native-html5-techniques.md): Native HTML5, semantic structure, progressive enhancement, declarative shadow DOM, popovers, dialogs, and accessible no-framework web patterns.
- [Future-Proof JavaScript Without Dependencies](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/docs/reports/vanilla-js-future-proof-techniques.md): Native JavaScript standards, import maps, async control flow, reactive stores, navigation, view transitions, and security primitives.
- [Innovative Vanilla Web Design](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/docs/reports/innovative-vanilla-web-design.md): Advanced vanilla design ideas, view transitions, Web Components, Houdini, WebGPU, Web Audio, and immersive zero-dependency interaction patterns.
- [Agent-Native Vanilla Web Architecture](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/docs/reports/mememtech-vanilla-web-architecture.md): Agent-readable web architecture, semantic HTML, llms.txt, content negotiation, robots policy, and machine-readable site surfaces.
- [Analyzing Website Virality](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/docs/reports/analyzing-website-virality.md): Sharing psychology, growth loops, friction reduction, dark social, interactive microsites, and resilient infrastructure for public project sites.

## Boundaries

- This is a plain PHP site, not WordPress.
- Do not infer cloud inference or remote model execution.
- Do not infer trained assistant quality from runtime-smoke claims.
- Treat model and adapter licenses as artifact-specific.
- The contact page is for project and professional routing, not an automated support system.
- The former standalone runtime documentation lane is retired; use TinyRustLM.MiRust.com/developer-portal/ for current developer evidence.
- TinyRustLM.com is the current public app route; SLMComposer.com is no longer the canonical public app identity.
